pages.title: Introduction
pages.text: The introduction of Vectorman (BlueSky Software, 1995) has a tune of its own, about two minutes long. The story that it introduces begins in 2049, when humans have left a polluted Earth and the machines called Orbots clean up after them.

pages.title: The robot who went mad
pages.text: In the story of Vectorman, Raster is a high-level Orbot who watches Earth through a planetwide computer network. A lesser Orbot accidentally attaches him to a working nuclear missile, and he goes insane and calls himself Warhead. Vectorman, a sludge barge pilot, comes back from dumping sludge in the sun and finds the other Orbots under Warhead's control.

pages.title: A game against television
pages.text: Richard Karpp, a designer of Vectorman, said that in the first discussions of the story, "we wanted a main theme for the game to be that passive entertainment, like television, was inferior to interactive entertainment". The plot ended up like the 1987 film The Running Man, with a deadly TV show. One trace of the idea remains in the game: Karpp says "you destroy a lot of TVs to get powerups".
